meta.title: Ceres Power — Phil Caldwell's solid oxide fuel cell licensing model from Horsham through Bosch, Doosan, Weichai, Shell partnerships
meta.abstract: Ceres Power Holdings plc is a UK clean-energy technology company listed on the London Stock Exchange AIM (CWR.L) developing solid oxide fuel cell (SOFC) and solid oxide electrolyser cell (SOEC) technology — its principal commercial model is licensing the SteelCell platform to global manufacturing partners including Bosch (Germany), Doosan (Korea), Weichai Power (China), and partnership with Shell on green hydrogen electrolysis. Headquartered in Horsham UK with the principal engineering site in Redhill UK. CEO Phil Caldwell has led the company through the licensing-model strategic pivot.

chapters.title: Snapshot
chapters.body:
## Capital-Light on the Main Market

Ceres Power Holdings plc occupied a narrow but distinctive position in the energy transition. It owned the intellectual property for metal-supported solid oxide fuel cell and electrolyser platforms, licensed that technology to industrial partners, and did not build gigafactories itself. By the frozen snapshot date of 23 May 2026, it was quoted on the Main Market of the London Stock Exchange, having moved up from AIM in June 2023, and remained headquartered in Horsham with its engineering campus in Redhill.[Ceres history](https://www.ceres.tech/who-we-are/our-history/) [Ceres leadership](https://www.ceres.tech/who-we-are/leadership/)

The company traced to a 2001 spin-out from Imperial College London. Ceres' own history page said the founding technology was based on Professor Brian Steele's work on doped-ceria electrolyte materials and a metal-supported solid oxide architecture designed to lower operating temperature and improve thermal-cycling robustness.[Ceres history](https://www.ceres.tech/who-we-are/our-history/)

Phil Caldwell, appointed chief executive on 2 September 2013, spent the next decade recasting the business from would-be manufacturer into licensor. The strategy rested on the idea that the value sat in the cell, the stack design and the process know-how, while the capital burden of factories could be pushed onto larger industrial partners.[Ceres leadership](https://www.ceres.tech/who-we-are/leadership/) [Ceres history](https://www.ceres.tech/who-we-are/our-history/)

## The Partner System After Bosch

The old shorthand of "Bosch, Doosan, Weichai and Shell" had become too narrow by the frozen window. Bosch had been the original European anchor, but on 20 February 2025 Ceres said Robert Bosch GmbH would discontinue its SOFC industrialisation activity, seek to end the partnership in an orderly way, and divest its 17.44 per cent stake. Ceres also said that consensus expectations for 2025 were unchanged.[Bosch statement](https://www.ceres.tech/media/ebeau4bp/ceres-statement-regarding-robert-bosch-gmbh.pdf)

The replacement story was not a single new partner. It was a broader ecosystem. Doosan Fuel Cell began mass production in South Korea in July 2025 at a facility with 50MW of annual electrical-generating capacity, becoming the first Ceres licensee to manufacture at scale and generating Ceres' first royalties.[Doosan joint announcement](https://www.ceres.tech/newsroom/news-and-insights/doosan-fuel-cell-begins-mass-production-of-fuel-cell-power-systems-using-ceres-technology/) The 2025 annual report recorded those first royalties at £110,000.[Ceres Annual Report 2025](https://www.ceres.tech/media/lponbtjc/ceres_annual-report_2025.pdf)

Weichai moved from long-standing strategic shareholder to manufacturing licensee. On 5 November 2025 Ceres announced a manufacturing licence for SOFC cells and stacks in China aimed at AI data centres, commercial buildings and industrial power markets.[Weichai manufacturing licence](https://www.ceres.tech/newsroom/news-and-insights/weichai-sign-manufacturing-licence-for-sofc-power/) Delta Electronics had already signed a roughly £43 million technology-transfer and licensing agreement in January 2024 covering both SOFC and SOEC applications, with production targeted by the end of 2026.[Delta-Ceres joint release](https://www.ceres.tech/media/ajfpxozk/180124-cwr-combined-rns-and-press-release.pdf) By July 2025 Delta had gone further, buying land and factory facilities in Taiwan for about NT$6.95 billion for large-scale hydrogen-energy manufacturing using Ceres technology.[Delta factory investment](https://www.ceres.tech/newsroom/news-and-insights/ceres-welcomes-delta-electronics-investment-in-factory-site-for-solid-oxide-hydrogen-energy-solutions/)

The SOEC side broadened as well. DENSO was disclosed in August 2024 as a long-term licence partner for Ceres' solid oxide electrolyser cells, with the agreement structured to include licence fees, engineering services, hardware and future royalties.[DENSO licence](https://www.ceres.tech/newsroom/news-and-insights/ceres-confirms-denso-as-the-latest-licence-partner/) Thermax followed in September 2024 with a non-exclusive global licence to manufacture, sell and service SOEC stack array modules in India.[Thermax licence](https://www.ceres.tech/news/thermax-partners-with-ceres-for-green-hydrogen-production-with-large-scale-solid-oxide-electrolysis-soec-manufacturing-in-india/) In March 2026 Ceres added Centrica as a service-led commercial channel for multi-gigawatt on-site power across the UK and Europe, and Delta was then disclosed as the manufacturing partner in that model.[Centrica-Ceres partnership](https://www.ceres.tech/newsroom/news-and-insights/centrica-and-ceres-sign-strategic-partnership-to-bring-multi-gw-on-site-fuel-power-to-the-uk-and-europe/) [Centrica-Delta partnership](https://www.ceres.tech/newsroom/news-and-insights/centrica-and-delta-electronics-announce-partnership/)

## Shell and the SOEC Proof Point

Shell remained the most visible validation of Ceres' electrolyser pathway. In June 2024 Ceres said Shell had awarded a second-phase contract to cooperate on the design of a solid oxide electrolyser module for large industrial applications.[Shell phase-two contract](https://www.ceres.tech/newsroom/news-and-insights/ceres-signs-contract-with-shell-for-green-hydrogen/) In May 2025 the companies announced first hydrogen production at Shell's 1MW demonstrator in Bangalore. Ceres said the system achieved module efficiency of 37 kWh/kg H2 and could produce as much as 600 kilograms of hydrogen a day at full operation.[Shell Bangalore milestone](https://www.ceres.tech/newsroom/news-and-insights/shell-ceres-mw-scale-electrolyser-project-produces-first-hydrogen/)

That did not mean Shell had become the missing manufacturing licensee. By the frozen date, Shell was still a demonstrator and development partner rather than a disclosed production licensee. The manufacturing side of the SOEC thesis had instead been built out through Delta, DENSO and Thermax, while AtkinsRealis had been working with Ceres since February 2024 on a 100MW-plus modularised hydrogen-production blueprint.[AtkinsRealis FEED](https://www.ceres.tech/newsroom/news-and-insights/ceres-and-atkinsrealis-to-design-modularised-green-hydrogen-production-system/)

## Financial Snapshot (FY 2025)

| Metric | FY 2025 | FY 2024 |
|---|---:|---:|
| Revenue | £32.6m | £51.9m |
| Gross profit / margin | £22.7m / 70% | £40.2m / 77% |
| Adjusted EBITDA loss | £(32.5)m | £(22.3)m |
| Cash, cash equivalents and short-term investments | £83.3m | £102.5m |
| Cash outflow | £(19.2)m | £(37.5)m |
| Royalties recognised | £0.11m | - |
| Current contracted group revenue for 2026 | ~£45m | - |

Those figures came from Ceres' March 2026 final-results statement and 2025 annual report.[FY2025 final results](https://www.ceres.tech/media/jpmpucda/ceres-power-holdings-plc-final-results-statement-2026-march-26.pdf) [Ceres Annual Report 2025](https://www.ceres.tech/media/lponbtjc/ceres_annual-report_2025.pdf) The revenue decline from 2024 reflected the absence of the unusually large up-front technology-transfer recognitions that had flattered the prior year. Yet deferred commercial visibility increased: contract liabilities rose to £23.284 million from £10.682 million, and the annual report said expected revenue from unsatisfied or partially unsatisfied performance obligations was £39.873 million for 2026, £21.624 million for 2027 and £12.026 million for 2028, excluding future contingent milestones and royalties.[Ceres Annual Report 2025](https://www.ceres.tech/media/lponbtjc/ceres_annual-report_2025.pdf)

## Open Questions

Four tensions still defined the dossier at the frozen date. First, whether Doosan's 50MW factory and Weichai's new manufacturing licence would scale fast enough to turn first royalties into material income.[Doosan joint announcement](https://www.ceres.tech/newsroom/news-and-insights/doosan-fuel-cell-begins-mass-production-of-fuel-cell-power-systems-using-ceres-technology/) [Weichai manufacturing licence](https://www.ceres.tech/newsroom/news-and-insights/weichai-sign-manufacturing-licence-for-sofc-power/) Second, whether the SOEC demonstrator pathway around Shell, Delta, DENSO and Thermax would mature into the same sort of repeatable manufacturing flywheel that Ceres had long promised on the fuel-cell side.[Shell Bangalore milestone](https://www.ceres.tech/newsroom/news-and-insights/shell-ceres-mw-scale-electrolyser-project-produces-first-hydrogen/) [DENSO licence](https://www.ceres.tech/newsroom/news-and-insights/ceres-confirms-denso-as-the-latest-licence-partner/) [Thermax licence](https://www.ceres.tech/news/thermax-partners-with-ceres-for-green-hydrogen-production-with-large-scale-solid-oxide-electrolysis-soec-manufacturing-in-india/)

Third, whether £83.3 million of cash and short-term investments was sufficient to bridge the business to multi-partner royalty scale without a further equity raise.[Ceres Annual Report 2025](https://www.ceres.tech/media/lponbtjc/ceres_annual-report_2025.pdf) And fourth, whether Ceres' licensing model would be rewarded as an IP platform or discounted because execution sat in the hands of partners. By May 2026 the model no longer looked hypothetical. It still looked early.

chapters.title: From 2001 Imperial College spin-out through the SteelCell licensing model pivot
chapters.body:
## The Laboratory Roots, 2001

Ceres Power did not begin with a licensing model. It began with a laboratory breakthrough at Imperial College London. The founding steel-substrate insight — depositing thin-film ceramic electrolytes onto ferritic stainless steel rather than brittle yttria-stabilised zirconia — would define every major strategic decision the company made over the following two decades. If it worked at scale, the SteelCell could be manufactured by any competent metalworking firm rather than a specialist ceramics house.

## The Direct Commercialisation Era

For much of the first decade after listing, Ceres pursued the more intuitive path: it would develop the technology to the point of commercial readiness and sell finished products. The most visible expression of this strategy was the micro-combined-heat-and-power market — residential systems, sold through partnerships with energy utilities, that would sit inside domestic boilers and generate electricity alongside heat. The company entered a commercial relationship with Centrica, British Gas's parent, exploring integration of fuel cell modules into home heating units.

The residential CHP vision was not obviously wrong. Japan's ENE-FARM programme, backed by Osaka Gas and Tokyo Gas, had demonstrated that fuel cells could find a consumer market as premium home appliances. But the capital requirements for Ceres to manufacture its way to meaningful volume were severe, and the economics of residential deployment in the UK — where gas prices remained relatively low and grid electricity cheap — made the payback calculations difficult. By the early 2010s, the Centrica relationship had wound down without producing commercial volumes.

The company's AIM-listed shares reflected the uncertainty. Multiple equity raises kept the balance sheet funded through the technology development years, but the stock consistently traded at a deep discount to the capital invested in the underlying science.

## The Caldwell Pivot

Phil Caldwell joined as chief executive in 2013 and concluded that Ceres was not a manufacturer but a technology licensor. The SteelCell's compatibility with standard metalworking processes meant established manufacturers could produce cells at cost structures Ceres could never achieve independently. The correct business model was to develop and defend the intellectual property, collect licence fees and engineering services revenue while partners scaled, and then transition to per-unit royalties as manufacturing volumes grew.

The pivot required a different organisation, a different balance sheet discipline, and a different kind of commercial relationship. Ceres would stop trying to build factories and start building a network of licensed partners whose installed manufacturing capacity would function as a distributed, capital-light extension of its own balance sheet. Caldwell's engineering background gave him credibility in technical negotiations; his commercial instincts framed the pitch around partners' industrial capabilities.

## Bosch: The Anchor Partnership

Bosch validated the licensing model in the mid-2010s. The German conglomerate's commitment went beyond a contractual licence — it took an equity stake in Ceres, providing both a credible route to industrial-scale manufacture and a shareholder whose interests aligned with long-term commercial build-out. For Bosch, access to a differentiated SOFC platform offered entry into distributed power generation and data-centre backup markets. The structure — front-loaded services income, back-loaded royalty potential — became the template for every subsequent partnership.

## Doosan and the Korean Expansion

Doosan Corporation extended the SteelCell's geographic footprint into a market with significant appetite for clean distributed generation driven by both industrial demand and Korean government energy policy. The partnership demonstrated that the SteelCell's steel-substrate design could be replicated across different industrial manufacturing ecosystems — a critical proof point for the licensing model's scalability thesis.

## Weichai and the China Opportunity

Weichai Power, the Chinese powertrain conglomerate, signed a partnership including significant equity investment in Ceres. The deal represented entry into a deployment environment where volumes could be of a different order of magnitude than Western markets. The equity component gave the relationship strategic weight, reducing the risk of dissolution if near-term deployment timelines slipped.

## Shell and the SOEC Expansion

Shell's partnership on solid oxide electrolyser cell technology brought Ceres into the green hydrogen production value chain. SOEC diversified the technology narrative beyond stationary fuel cells at a moment when hydrogen was attracting significant capital market interest.

## The Model's Internal Logic

By the early 2020s, Ceres had assembled a partner network spanning four major industrial manufacturing ecosystems. The SteelCell's core advantage — compatibility with existing metalworking production infrastructure — had enabled partnerships that a ceramic-based SOFC design almost certainly could not have secured at comparable speed or cost.

The financial architecture remained one of managed cash consumption while waiting for partner royalty volumes to arrive at commercial scale. Multiple equity raises kept the balance sheet solvent through extended development periods. Caldwell's consistent message was that Ceres's value resided in the IP and the partner network, not in manufacturing footprint — and that the royalty inflection, when it came, would reflect aggregate partner deployments measured in units, not laboratory cells.

The logic was coherent. Its execution, spread across multiple geographies and subject to the political and industrial cycles of the global hydrogen transition, would test its durability in the years that followed.

chapters.title: SteelCell SOFC platform, SOEC electrolysis, and the licensing model
chapters.body:
## The Steel Substrate Differentiator

In a standard solid oxide cell, mechanical support and electrochemical function are carried by a largely ceramic structure. Ceres' design inverted that logic. Its core product page said the cell used a steel-supported design operating in a "Goldilocks" range of roughly 450-630C, allowing the use of lower-cost materials while improving robustness to cycling and emergency stops.[Ceres cell](https://www.ceres.tech/products-and-applications/products/cell/) [Goldilocks zone](https://www.ceres.tech/newsroom/news-and-insights/the-goldilocks-zone-how-ceres-has-optimised-solid-oxide/)

That materials choice underpinned the commercial pitch. Because the ceramic functional layers were printed on ferritic steel rather than a thick all-ceramic support, Ceres argued that the product could be manufactured with processes far closer to mainstream metalworking than to specialist ceramic fabrication.[Ceres cell](https://www.ceres.tech/products-and-applications/products/cell/) [Cell to system explained](https://www.ceres.tech/newsroom/news-and-insights/cell-to-system-explained/)

The latest product disclosures framed the performance more aggressively than the older dossier language had. On its stack and Endura product pages, Ceres said the platform could deliver about 69 per cent electrical efficiency on natural gas at stack level, more than 65 per cent electrical efficiency in power generation, and more than 90 per cent total efficiency in combined-heat-and-power applications.[Ceres stack](https://www.ceres.tech/products-and-applications/products/stack/) [Ceres Endura](https://www.ceres.tech/newsroom/news-and-insights/ceres-launches-ceres-endura/)

## SOEC: Running the Reaction in Reverse

The same platform was being pushed into electrolysis. Ceres described its SOEC offering as a reversible use of the same core cell and stack technology, with hydrogen-production economics helped by higher operating temperatures and lower electricity demand than low-temperature alternatives when integrated properly with heat.[Ceres cell](https://www.ceres.tech/products-and-applications/products/cell/) [Why Ceres' SOEC has the lowest cost potential](https://www.ceres.tech/newsroom/news-and-insights/why-ceres-solid-oxide-electrolyser-has-the-lowest-cost-potential/)

Shell's Bangalore demonstrator made that more than a laboratory claim. By June 2025 the system had produced first hydrogen, and Ceres said it had exceeded performance expectations at 37 kWh/kg H2.[Shell Bangalore milestone](https://www.ceres.tech/newsroom/news-and-insights/shell-ceres-mw-scale-electrolyser-project-produces-first-hydrogen/)

## The Licensing Architecture

A typical Ceres relationship moved through recognisable stages. A partner first took a licence for a geography or application. Engineering services and hardware revenue followed as Ceres supported technology transfer and product development. Milestone receipts created periodic jumps in revenue recognition. Only after commercial production did the royalty line begin to appear. The 2025 annual report showed that this long-promised final stage had at last started, albeit modestly, with Doosan's first royalty payments.[Ceres Annual Report 2025](https://www.ceres.tech/media/lponbtjc/ceres_annual-report_2025.pdf)

The capital-light character was still real. Ceres' product and factory pages said the company had built a UK pilot plant but was supporting the development of partner factories globally rather than carrying large manufacturing assets itself.[Ceres factory](https://www.ceres.tech/products-and-applications/products/factory/) The 2025 balance sheet accordingly remained far lighter than that of a vertically integrated OEM, with the principal investment still concentrated in engineering capability, product development and technology transfer.[Ceres Annual Report 2025](https://www.ceres.tech/media/lponbtjc/ceres_annual-report_2025.pdf)

The contrast with Bloom Energy remained sharp. Bloom manufactured and sold directly; Ceres licensed and supported partners. One model captured the customer relationship and the installed-base service annuity directly. The other aimed to spread the same technology across multiple industrial balance sheets without funding factories itself.[Bloom FY2025 results](https://investor.bloomenergy.com/press-releases/press-release-details/2026/Bloom-Energy-Reports-Fourth-Quarter-and-Full-Year-2025-Financial-Results-with-Record-Full-Year-Revenues/default.aspx)

| Dimension | Ceres Power | Bloom Energy |
|---|---|---|
| Business model | Capital-light licensing and royalties | Vertical manufacturing and direct sale/service |
| Core platform | Solid oxide for power generation and electrolysis | Solid oxide for power generation and electrolysis |
| Manufacturing posture at the frozen date | Partner-operated factories and product lines | Proprietary manufacturing |
| Commercial control | Shared with partners and channels | Held directly by Bloom |

## Partners as Revenue Engines

By the frozen date the partner map had become broader than the old Bosch-Doosan-Weichai-Shell frame. On the power side, Doosan had entered mass production in Korea, Weichai had signed a manufacturing licence in China, Delta had licensed both SOFC and SOEC technology in Taiwan, and Centrica had become a service-led route to market in the UK and Europe.[Doosan joint announcement](https://www.ceres.tech/newsroom/news-and-insights/doosan-fuel-cell-begins-mass-production-of-fuel-cell-power-systems-using-ceres-technology/) [Weichai manufacturing licence](https://www.ceres.tech/newsroom/news-and-insights/weichai-sign-manufacturing-licence-for-sofc-power/) [Delta-Ceres joint release](https://www.ceres.tech/media/ajfpxozk/180124-cwr-combined-rns-and-press-release.pdf) [Centrica-Ceres partnership](https://www.ceres.tech/newsroom/news-and-insights/centrica-and-ceres-sign-strategic-partnership-to-bring-multi-gw-on-site-fuel-power-to-the-uk-and-europe/)

On the hydrogen side, DENSO and Thermax had joined Shell and Delta as disclosed SOEC partners, while AtkinsRealis was designing a modularised 100MW-plus system architecture.[DENSO licence](https://www.ceres.tech/newsroom/news-and-insights/ceres-confirms-denso-as-the-latest-licence-partner/) [Thermax licence](https://www.ceres.tech/news/thermax-partners-with-ceres-for-green-hydrogen-production-with-large-scale-solid-oxide-electrolysis-soec-manufacturing-in-india/) [AtkinsRealis FEED](https://www.ceres.tech/newsroom/news-and-insights/ceres-and-atkinsrealis-to-design-modularised-green-hydrogen-production-system/) Bosch, by contrast, had moved out of the current manufacturing set once it decided in February 2025 to discontinue SOFC industrialisation activity.[Bosch statement](https://www.ceres.tech/media/ebeau4bp/ceres-statement-regarding-robert-bosch-gmbh.pdf)

That left the core business-model question unchanged but better grounded. Ceres had shown that one factory design, one stack family and one engineering organisation could be transferred into several industrial contexts. The unresolved question was not whether the architecture was licensable. It was whether the aggregate royalty line would expand fast enough to justify the patience the model demanded.

chapters.title: Revenue mix, cash burn, partner royalty trajectory
chapters.body:
## The Revenue Stack: Fees First, Royalties Later

Ceres' reported income had always been easier to misunderstand than to dismiss. The company was not a pre-revenue science project by the mid-2020s; nor was it yet a royalty machine. The disclosed pattern was a sequence of licence fees, engineering-services revenue, hardware supply and milestone payments that rose and fell with partner progress. Royalties were always meant to be the destination, not the starting point.[Ceres Annual Report 2025](https://www.ceres.tech/media/lponbtjc/ceres_annual-report_2025.pdf)

Two accounting points mattered before any table was read. First, Ceres changed its year-end from 30 June to 31 December in 2020, so the 2020 annual report covered an 18-month period rather than a normal financial year.[Ceres Annual Report 2020](https://www.ceres.tech/media/4z2ir5um/cpl001_ar_for-web-1.pdf) Second, the 2023 annual report restated 2021 and 2022 revenue after identifying historical timing and foreign-exchange errors on legacy long-term contracts. Management said those adjustments reduced revenue by £1.7 million in 2021 and £2.3 million in 2022.[Ceres Annual Report 2023](https://www.ceres.tech/media/vfdfoi04/ceres-annual-report-2023-continuous-spreads-1.pdf)

## Revenue by Period: What the Disclosures Actually Showed

| Period | Reported revenue | Mix disclosed in the primary source |
|---|---:|---|
| 12 months to 30 Jun 2019 | £15.300m | Engineering services £6.437m; hardware £1.451m; licences £7.412m |
| 18 months to 31 Dec 2020 | £31.682m | Engineering services £10.866m; hardware £10.297m; licences £10.519m |
| FY2021 | £31.7m revenue and other income | Annual report said growth was driven principally by licence-fee income, mainly from Doosan |
| FY2022 (restated) | £19.788m | Engineering services £9.039m; hardware £5.380m; licences £5.369m |
| FY2023 | £22.324m | Engineering services £10.220m; hardware £5.726m; licences £6.378m |
| FY2024 | £51.891m | Hardware £6.938m; engineering services and licences £44.953m |
| FY2025 | £32.643m | Hardware £14.328m; engineering services and licences £18.315m; royalties £0.110m |

The figures came from Ceres' 2020, 2021, 2023, 2024 and 2025 annual reports.[Ceres Annual Report 2020](https://www.ceres.tech/media/4z2ir5um/cpl001_ar_for-web-1.pdf) [Ceres Annual Report 2021](https://www.ceres.tech/media/4pbl4ffn/2021-annual-report_ceres-power-holdings-plc.pdf) [Ceres Annual Report 2023](https://www.ceres.tech/media/vfdfoi04/ceres-annual-report-2023-continuous-spreads-1.pdf) [Ceres Annual Report 2024](https://www.ceres.tech/media/pyqnbj5r/ceres-annual-report-and-accounts-2024.pdf) [Ceres Annual Report 2025](https://www.ceres.tech/media/lponbtjc/ceres_annual-report_2025.pdf)

The pattern was plain. Reported revenue existed and, in some years, was substantial. But it was not yet recurring in the way a mature semiconductor-IP royalty line would have been. It was tied to technology transfer, partner engineering support and the timing of milestone gates. That was why 2024 could jump to £51.891 million and 2025 could fall back to £32.643 million without any corresponding collapse in strategic activity.[Ceres Annual Report 2024](https://www.ceres.tech/media/pyqnbj5r/ceres-annual-report-and-accounts-2024.pdf) [Ceres Annual Report 2025](https://www.ceres.tech/media/lponbtjc/ceres_annual-report_2025.pdf)

## Equity Capital and the Runway Question

The balance sheet was reinforced not only by placings but by strategic partners. Weichai's 2018 strategic partnership brought a 20 per cent equity investment for £48 million and gave Ceres access to the Chinese market.[Weichai strategic partnership](https://www.ceres.tech/newsroom/news-and-insights/strategic-partnership-with-weichai-power/) Bosch first entered in 2018 and then, in January 2020, increased its stake from about 4 per cent to about 18 per cent through a £77.3 million transaction, of which £38 million was gross proceeds to Ceres and the rest went to existing shareholders.[Bosch increases stake](https://www.ceres.tech/media/b4plszm3/bosch-increases-its-stake-in-ceres.pdf)

By 31 December 2025, the capital structure had evolved again. The annual report showed 194,694,543 ordinary shares outstanding, with Weichai Power (Hong Kong) International Development Co., Ltd. still the largest identified shareholder on 37,965,262 shares, or 19.49 per cent.[Ceres Annual Report 2025](https://www.ceres.tech/media/lponbtjc/ceres_annual-report_2025.pdf) Bosch, by contrast, had already said in February 2025 that it intended to divest its 17.44 per cent position as it exited SOFC industrialisation.[Bosch statement](https://www.ceres.tech/media/ebeau4bp/ceres-statement-regarding-robert-bosch-gmbh.pdf)

## The Royalty Column Finally Appeared

The symbolic change in 2025 was that the royalty line stopped being theoretical. Doosan's South Korean factory began mass production in July 2025 with 50MW of annual capacity, and Ceres booked £110,000 of royalties for the year.[Doosan joint announcement](https://www.ceres.tech/newsroom/news-and-insights/doosan-fuel-cell-begins-mass-production-of-fuel-cell-power-systems-using-ceres-technology/) [Ceres Annual Report 2025](https://www.ceres.tech/media/lponbtjc/ceres_annual-report_2025.pdf) That was financially small but analytically important: it demonstrated that the accounting bridge from engineering support to volume-linked royalties did in fact exist.

The next revenue layers were already visible in disclosure. Weichai signed a manufacturing licence in November 2025, and Ceres said current contracted group revenue for 2026 was about £45 million before any new business.[Weichai manufacturing licence](https://www.ceres.tech/newsroom/news-and-insights/weichai-sign-manufacturing-licence-for-sofc-power/) [FY2025 final results](https://www.ceres.tech/media/jpmpucda/ceres-power-holdings-plc-final-results-statement-2026-march-26.pdf) The 2025 annual report also showed contract liabilities rising to £23.284 million from £10.682 million, while expected revenue from unsatisfied or partially unsatisfied obligations stood at £39.873 million for 2026, £21.624 million for 2027 and £12.026 million for 2028, excluding contingent milestones and future royalties.[Ceres Annual Report 2025](https://www.ceres.tech/media/lponbtjc/ceres_annual-report_2025.pdf)

## SOEC Added Optionality, Not Stability

On the electrolyser side, the same financial logic applied. Delta's January 2024 agreement, DENSO's August 2024 licence, Thermax's September 2024 licence and Shell's continuing development work all expanded the addressable revenue base, but they did so first through licence, engineering and hardware flows rather than through immediate commercial royalties.[Delta-Ceres joint release](https://www.ceres.tech/media/ajfpxozk/180124-cwr-combined-rns-and-press-release.pdf) [DENSO licence](https://www.ceres.tech/newsroom/news-and-insights/ceres-confirms-denso-as-the-latest-licence-partner/) [Thermax licence](https://www.ceres.tech/news/thermax-partners-with-ceres-for-green-hydrogen-production-with-large-scale-solid-oxide-electrolysis-soec-manufacturing-in-india/) [Shell phase-two contract](https://www.ceres.tech/newsroom/news-and-insights/ceres-signs-contract-with-shell-for-green-hydrogen/)

That was why the financial deep dive still came back to the same question. Ceres had proved it could sign world-class partners and monetise that through engineering and technology-transfer revenues. The unresolved issue at the frozen date was not whether the model generated revenue. It was how quickly the royalty share of that revenue could widen.

chapters.title: Multi-year trajectory through partner scaling and SOEC entry
chapters.body:
## From Milestone Accounting to the First Royalty Line

Ceres' earnings story was not a smooth revenue-growth curve. It was a record of partner progression, contract timing and an eventual move from fee income toward royalties. That made the sequence of annual reports more useful than half-year snapshots or transcript rhetoric.

One mechanical issue mattered immediately. Ceres changed its reporting year-end in 2020, so the 2020 annual report covered an 18-month period through 31 December 2020.[Ceres Annual Report 2020](https://www.ceres.tech/media/4z2ir5um/cpl001_ar_for-web-1.pdf) A second issue emerged later: in 2023 the company restated 2021 and 2022 revenue after identifying errors in the historical timing of licence revenue and related foreign-exchange effects. Management said the corrections reduced revenue by £1.7 million in 2021 and £2.3 million in 2022.[Ceres Annual Report 2023](https://www.ceres.tech/media/vfdfoi04/ceres-annual-report-2023-continuous-spreads-1.pdf)

## What the Annual Results Actually Said

| Reporting year | Revenue | Gross profit / margin | What moved the number |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| FY2021 | £31.7m revenue and other income | 66% gross margin | Annual report said growth was driven principally by licence-fee income, mainly from Doosan |
| FY2022 (restated) | £19.788m | £10.709m / 54% | Lower milestone recognition after the 2021 peak |
| FY2023 | £22.324m | £13.554m / 61% | Existing-partner revenue plus correction of prior-period errors |
| FY2024 | £51.891m | £40.2m / 77% | Large technology-transfer and licence recognition, including Delta-related work |
| FY2025 | £32.643m | £22.7m / 70% | Lower up-front recognitions, offset partly by the first royalties |

The source documents were the 2021, 2023, 2024 and 2025 annual reports.[Ceres Annual Report 2021](https://www.ceres.tech/media/4pbl4ffn/2021-annual-report_ceres-power-holdings-plc.pdf) [Ceres Annual Report 2023](https://www.ceres.tech/media/vfdfoi04/ceres-annual-report-2023-continuous-spreads-1.pdf) [Ceres Annual Report 2024](https://www.ceres.tech/media/pyqnbj5r/ceres-annual-report-and-accounts-2024.pdf) [Ceres Annual Report 2025](https://www.ceres.tech/media/lponbtjc/ceres_annual-report_2025.pdf)

The 2021 report marked the point at which Ceres could credibly say it had both commercial traction and liquidity. It reported £31.7 million of revenue and other income and £250 million of cash, cash equivalents and investments after the March 2021 fund-raise.[Ceres Annual Report 2021](https://www.ceres.tech/media/4pbl4ffn/2021-annual-report_ceres-power-holdings-plc.pdf) But that apparent smoothness later needed qualification because the 2023 restatement showed part of the old 2021 and 2022 revenue base had been recognised too early.[Ceres Annual Report 2023](https://www.ceres.tech/media/vfdfoi04/ceres-annual-report-2023-continuous-spreads-1.pdf)

## 2023: Clean-Up Year, Not Collapse

The 2023 result mattered less for its headline than for what it clarified. Revenue came in at £22.324 million against restated 2022 revenue of £19.788 million, while gross profit rose to £13.554 million and gross margin to 61 per cent.[Ceres Annual Report 2023](https://www.ceres.tech/media/vfdfoi04/ceres-annual-report-2023-continuous-spreads-1.pdf) The report also made clear that Shell's test-and-evaluation partnership was expected to start generating revenue once the Bangalore demonstrator was commissioned in 2024.[Ceres Annual Report 2023](https://www.ceres.tech/media/vfdfoi04/ceres-annual-report-2023-continuous-spreads-1.pdf)

That year also cleaned up the record around prior revenue recognition. What looked, in older narrative summaries, like a simple slowdown was in part an accounting correction. For anyone reading the longer earnings arc, 2023 was the reset point from which the later 2024-2025 comparison needed to be judged.

## 2024: The Licence Model at Full Stretch

The 2024 annual report showed what the model looked like when large partner recognitions landed in one year. Revenue jumped to £51.891 million from £22.324 million, while gross profit reached £40.2 million and gross margin 77 per cent.[Ceres Annual Report 2024](https://www.ceres.tech/media/pyqnbj5r/ceres-annual-report-and-accounts-2024.pdf) The report no longer split engineering services and licences separately in its major product-line presentation, but it showed £44.953 million from those combined lines against £6.938 million of hardware.[Ceres Annual Report 2024](https://www.ceres.tech/media/pyqnbj5r/ceres-annual-report-and-accounts-2024.pdf)

Commercially, 2024 was also the year the SOEC franchise broadened. Delta signed its £43 million collaboration in January, DENSO was confirmed in August, and Thermax followed in September.[Delta-Ceres joint release](https://www.ceres.tech/media/ajfpxozk/180124-cwr-combined-rns-and-press-release.pdf) [DENSO licence](https://www.ceres.tech/newsroom/news-and-insights/ceres-confirms-denso-as-the-latest-licence-partner/) [Thermax licence](https://www.ceres.tech/news/thermax-partners-with-ceres-for-green-hydrogen-production-with-large-scale-solid-oxide-electrolysis-soec-manufacturing-in-india/) The top line therefore did not simply reflect one partner or one market. It reflected a broader surge in technology-transfer activity.

## 2025: Lower Revenue, Better Proof

The 2025 result looked weaker on the headline but stronger on mechanism. Revenue fell back to £32.643 million from the 2024 peak and gross profit declined to £22.7 million, with margin at 70 per cent.[Ceres Annual Report 2025](https://www.ceres.tech/media/lponbtjc/ceres_annual-report_2025.pdf) Yet 2025 was the year Doosan began mass production and Ceres booked its first £110,000 of royalties.[Doosan joint announcement](https://www.ceres.tech/newsroom/news-and-insights/doosan-fuel-cell-begins-mass-production-of-fuel-cell-power-systems-using-ceres-technology/) [Ceres Annual Report 2025](https://www.ceres.tech/media/lponbtjc/ceres_annual-report_2025.pdf)

The results statement also said current contracted group revenue for 2026 was approximately £45 million before any new business.[FY2025 final results](https://www.ceres.tech/media/jpmpucda/ceres-power-holdings-plc-final-results-statement-2026-march-26.pdf) In other words, the company exited 2025 with a smaller headline revenue number than the year before, but with better evidence that partner production was beginning to translate into the royalty model management had spent years describing.

## The Earnings Story in Plain English

Read across the full period, the earnings story was not that Ceres had failed to grow. It was that growth had arrived first through partner-funded development work and only later through recurring unit economics. The sequence moved from liquidity and licence fees in 2021, to accounting clean-up and stabilisation in 2023, to a very strong but lumpy licence-and-milestone year in 2024, and finally to the first visible royalty proof in 2025.

That was why the dossier's old half-year heuristics were less useful than the disclosed annual pattern. Ceres' revenue floor still came from engineering and licensing activity. The earnings debate at the frozen date was about how soon that floor would be overtaken by royalties rather than whether those fees had ever existed.

chapters.title: Phil Caldwell, executive team, board, and partner shareholders
chapters.body:
## An Engineer at the Helm

Phil Caldwell did not arrive at Ceres as a chemist. He arrived as a chemical engineer. The company's leadership page said he had worked in the fuel-cell industry for 18 years before joining Ceres, including roles at Intelligent Energy and ICI, and held a master's degree in Chemical Engineering from Imperial College.[Ceres leadership](https://www.ceres.tech/who-we-are/leadership/)

His appointment date was 2 September 2013.[Ceres leadership](https://www.ceres.tech/who-we-are/leadership/) The timing mattered. Ceres' own history page recorded that British Gas had placed a forward order for 37,500 wall-mounted CHP units and taken a 10 per cent equity stake in 2007, then ended its investment in 2012.[Ceres history](https://www.ceres.tech/who-we-are/our-history/) Caldwell inherited the aftermath of that failed residential thesis and adopted the asset-light licensing model that remained the organising idea of the company through the frozen date.[Ceres history](https://www.ceres.tech/who-we-are/our-history/) [Ceres leadership](https://www.ceres.tech/who-we-are/leadership/)

Under his tenure the group moved from trying to commercialise its own products to transferring technology to industrial partners. By May 2026 that strategy had produced disclosed manufacturing or route-to-market relationships with Doosan, Weichai, Delta, DENSO, Thermax, Shell and Centrica, and had taken Ceres from AIM to the Main Market.[Ceres history](https://www.ceres.tech/who-we-are/our-history/) [Centrica-Ceres partnership](https://www.ceres.tech/newsroom/news-and-insights/centrica-and-ceres-sign-strategic-partnership-to-bring-multi-gw-on-site-fuel-power-to-the-uk-and-europe/)

## Engineering and Commercial Leadership

The senior team looked more industrial than promotional by the frozen date. Caroline Hargrove had joined as chief technology officer in 2021 after three years as a non-executive director; the leadership page said her background ran from Cambridge lecturing through McLaren F1 to Babylon Health, and noted that she had received a CBE for services to engineering.[Ceres leadership](https://www.ceres.tech/who-we-are/leadership/) Nick Lawrence, who joined in 2016, had become chief product officer after leading work across engineering, digitalisation, modelling and AI, and held an MEng in Engineering Science from Oxford.[Ceres leadership](https://www.ceres.tech/who-we-are/leadership/)

Stephen Hill became chief operating officer in summer 2025 after joining Ceres in 2007 as a manufacturing engineer. His official biography said he had overseen manufacturing operations, technology transfer to licence partners, quality, facilities, and health and safety.[Ceres leadership](https://www.ceres.tech/who-we-are/leadership/) That made him the executive most closely tied to the shift from laboratory process to partner factory. Filip Smeets, appointed chief commercial officer in September 2024, arrived from Nel Hydrogen, where Ceres said he had led the electrolyser division.[Ceres leadership](https://www.ceres.tech/who-we-are/leadership/) Stuart Paynter became CFO on 1 October 2024 after senior finance roles at Oxford Biomedica and Shire, and held a Physics degree from Imperial College plus chartered-accountant status.[Ceres leadership](https://www.ceres.tech/who-we-are/leadership/)

Michelle Traynor, chief people officer since 2019, rounded out the top team with responsibility for people strategy across a company that had shifted from research-heavy build-out toward commercial execution.[Ceres leadership](https://www.ceres.tech/who-we-are/leadership/) That role mattered more in 2025 than in earlier years because the final-results statement said a business-transformation plan had been implemented to align the company around commercial opportunities and deliver anticipated operating-cost savings of 20 per cent in 2026.[FY2025 final results](https://www.ceres.tech/media/jpmpucda/ceres-power-holdings-plc-final-results-statement-2026-march-26.pdf)

## The Board After Bosch

The older dossier had overstated the continuity of Bosch's influence and misstated Warren Finegold's timeline. Ceres' leadership page said Finegold joined the board as an independent non-executive director on 1 March 2020 and became chair in June 2020, not on the day he joined the board.[Ceres leadership](https://www.ceres.tech/who-we-are/leadership/) His background remained recognisably City and telecoms: Vodafone group executive committee, UBS investment banking, Oxford PPE and London Business School.[Ceres leadership](https://www.ceres.tech/who-we-are/leadership/)

The board composition by the frozen date also showed a more formal Main Market structure than the older AIM-era language implied. The leadership page identified Caroline Brown as chair of the Audit and Risk Committee, Julia King as senior independent director and chair of ESG, and Tudor Brown as chair of the Remuneration and Nomination Committee.[Ceres leadership](https://www.ceres.tech/who-we-are/leadership/) Karen Bomba and Trine Borum Bojsen added further industrial and energy-sector experience.[Ceres leadership](https://www.ceres.tech/who-we-are/leadership/)

The appointment dates underscored how much of the board had been refreshed around the Main Market transition. Tudor Brown joined on 1 April 2021, Julia King on 17 June 2021, Trine Borum Bojsen on 15 March 2022, and Caroline Brown and Karen Bomba on 1 June 2023.[Ceres leadership](https://www.ceres.tech/who-we-are/leadership/) That sequence was consistent with a company that was broadening from founder-era resilience into something closer to institutional public-company governance.

Bosch's formal governance role, however, had ended. Uwe Glock resigned from the board on 19 February 2025, and Ceres disclosed the next day that Bosch would discontinue its SOFC industrialisation activity, seek an orderly end to the partnership and divest its 17.44 per cent shareholding.[Ceres Annual Report 2025](https://www.ceres.tech/media/lponbtjc/ceres_annual-report_2025.pdf) [Bosch statement](https://www.ceres.tech/media/ebeau4bp/ceres-statement-regarding-robert-bosch-gmbh.pdf) The earlier suggestion that Glock's departure did not amount to a commercial rupture was therefore wrong. It coincided with Bosch's decision to step back from the business line entirely.

## Strategic Shareholders and Weichai's Board Seat

The old dossier also under-described Weichai's governance presence. Ceres' leadership page explicitly identified Nannan Sun as the Weichai-nominated non-executive director, appointed on 27 September 2023.[Ceres leadership](https://www.ceres.tech/who-we-are/leadership/) Her biography said she was assistant president of Weichai Power and president of its Future Technology Institute.[Ceres leadership](https://www.ceres.tech/who-we-are/leadership/)

That mattered because Weichai remained the largest disclosed shareholder. The 2025 annual report showed Weichai Power (Hong Kong) International Development Co., Ltd. holding 37,965,262 shares, equivalent to 19.49 per cent of issued share capital.[Ceres Annual Report 2025](https://www.ceres.tech/media/lponbtjc/ceres_annual-report_2025.pdf) Historically, Ceres' own records showed the relationship began with a 2018 strategic partnership, including a 20 per cent equity investment for £48 million and an initial focus on a 30kW range-extender system for Chinese buses.[Weichai strategic partnership](https://www.ceres.tech/newsroom/news-and-insights/strategic-partnership-with-weichai-power/) By November 2025 that had evolved into a manufacturing licence for stationary-power SOFC products in China.[Weichai manufacturing licence](https://www.ceres.tech/newsroom/news-and-insights/weichai-sign-manufacturing-licence-for-sofc-power/)

The same annual report showed the next-largest disclosed holders were Covalis Capital LLP on 9.65 per cent and M&G PLC on 4.76 per cent, while also stating that no shareholder qualified as a controlling shareholder under UK Listing Rule 6.6.1.[Ceres Annual Report 2025](https://www.ceres.tech/media/lponbtjc/ceres_annual-report_2025.pdf) That ownership mix mattered. It meant strategic influence was real, but it was not formally absolute.

Bosch's earlier shareholding also needed precision. The key 2020 step-up was not simply "another £48 million". Bosch's January 2020 transaction increased its stake from about 4 per cent to about 18 per cent in a £77.3 million deal, of which £38 million went to Ceres as new money and the rest to existing shareholders.[Bosch increases stake](https://www.ceres.tech/media/b4plszm3/bosch-increases-its-stake-in-ceres.pdf)

## Imperial, Awards and Institutional Credibility

The Imperial College thread remained real, but it was less mystical than the old version suggested. Ceres' history page said the company spun out from Imperial in 2001 to commercialise Brian Steele's metal-supported solid oxide research.[Ceres history](https://www.ceres.tech/who-we-are/our-history/) Caldwell and Paynter both held Imperial degrees, but the more tangible sign of institutional credibility by the frozen date was the accumulation of external recognition and partnerships.

Ceres won the MacRobert Award for Engineering Innovation in July 2023 and had previously received the Queen's Award for Enterprise in April 2021.[MacRobert Award](https://www.ceres.tech/newsroom/news-and-insights/ceres-wins-prestigious-macrobert-award-for-engineering-innovation/) [Ceres history](https://www.ceres.tech/who-we-are/our-history/) In January 2026 it announced a clean-power and hydrogen collaboration with the University of Surrey, suggesting the academic pipeline had remained alive well after the original spin-out phase.[University of Surrey collaboration](https://www.ceres.tech/newsroom/news-and-insights/ceres-and-university-of-surrey-partner-to-drive-innovation-in-clean-energy/)

The credibility story was not only symbolic. The 2025 annual report said the average number of employees fell to 462 from 546 in 2024, with year-end headcount at 353, as the company implemented its transformation plan.[Ceres Annual Report 2025](https://www.ceres.tech/media/lponbtjc/ceres_annual-report_2025.pdf) That made the leadership challenge less abstract: management was being asked not only to govern a portfolio of global partners, but to reshape the internal organisation without slowing product development or technology transfer.

## Governance at the Frozen Date

By May 2026, Ceres no longer fit the description of an AIM small-cap with loose governance. It had been on the Main Market since June 2023, had a board committee structure visible on its leadership materials, and had replaced Bosch's board influence with a more conventional independent-chair structure plus a disclosed Weichai-nominated director.[Ceres history](https://www.ceres.tech/who-we-are/our-history/) [Ceres leadership](https://www.ceres.tech/who-we-are/leadership/)

The residual governance questions were therefore narrower than in the earlier draft but not trivial. They concerned strategic-shareholder influence, concentration of institutional memory around Caldwell and a small executive team, the translation of board oversight into partner-factory execution, and the extent to which succession could be managed without diluting the relationship capital accumulated over more than a decade. Those were real issues. They were simply different from the ones the AIM-era framing had implied.

chapters.title: Bosch, Doosan, Weichai, Shell — the partner-customer base
chapters.body:
## The Architecture of the Partner Stack

Ceres' central commercial bet was that it would not become a manufacturer. Instead it would collect licence fees, engineering-services income, hardware revenue and, eventually, royalties as other companies manufactured products built around its solid oxide platform. By the frozen date that stack was broader than the old four-name shorthand suggested.[Ceres Annual Report 2025](https://www.ceres.tech/media/lponbtjc/ceres_annual-report_2025.pdf)

The partner base now fell into three buckets. First were fuel-cell manufacturing partners: Doosan in South Korea, Weichai in China and Delta in Taiwan.[Doosan joint announcement](https://www.ceres.tech/newsroom/news-and-insights/doosan-fuel-cell-begins-mass-production-of-fuel-cell-power-systems-using-ceres-technology/) [Weichai manufacturing licence](https://www.ceres.tech/newsroom/news-and-insights/weichai-sign-manufacturing-licence-for-sofc-power/) [Delta-Ceres joint release](https://www.ceres.tech/media/ajfpxozk/180124-cwr-combined-rns-and-press-release.pdf) Second were SOEC manufacturing partners and developers: Shell, DENSO, Thermax and Delta.[Shell Bangalore milestone](https://www.ceres.tech/newsroom/news-and-insights/shell-ceres-mw-scale-electrolyser-project-produces-first-hydrogen/) [DENSO licence](https://www.ceres.tech/newsroom/news-and-insights/ceres-confirms-denso-as-the-latest-licence-partner/) [Thermax licence](https://www.ceres.tech/news/thermax-partners-with-ceres-for-green-hydrogen-production-with-large-scale-solid-oxide-electrolysis-soec-manufacturing-in-india/) Third was route-to-market infrastructure, where Centrica had entered in 2026 to originate, install and service projects in the UK and Europe.[Centrica-Ceres partnership](https://www.ceres.tech/newsroom/news-and-insights/centrica-and-ceres-sign-strategic-partnership-to-bring-multi-gw-on-site-fuel-power-to-the-uk-and-europe/)

Bosch remained part of the history but not the current operating core. On 20 February 2025 Ceres said Bosch would discontinue SOFC industrialisation, seek an orderly end to the partnership and divest its 17.44 per cent shareholding.[Bosch statement](https://www.ceres.tech/media/ebeau4bp/ceres-statement-regarding-robert-bosch-gmbh.pdf)

## Bosch: From Anchor to Exit

Bosch was still the relationship that had validated the licensing model in the eyes of many investors. Ceres' history page showed Bosch first taking a stake in 2018 and then, in January 2020, increasing its holding materially while pushing toward industrial scale.[Ceres history](https://www.ceres.tech/who-we-are/our-history/) The January 2020 Bosch transaction took the group from roughly 4 per cent to roughly 18 per cent ownership in a £77.3 million deal.[Bosch increases stake](https://www.ceres.tech/media/b4plszm3/bosch-increases-its-stake-in-ceres.pdf)

But the frozen window captured the unwind rather than the build-out. Bosch's February 2025 statement said the SOFC market had not developed as expected for its strategy and that it would discontinue the activity.[Bosch statement](https://www.ceres.tech/media/ebeau4bp/ceres-statement-regarding-robert-bosch-gmbh.pdf) That changed Bosch from future catalyst to realised concentration risk.

## Doosan: The First Production Proof

If Bosch had been the old anchor, Doosan was the first working royalty proof. Ceres and Doosan announced on 28 July 2025 that Doosan Fuel Cell had begun mass production of fuel-cell power systems using Ceres technology at a dedicated South Korean factory capable of 50MW of annual electrical-generating capacity.[Doosan joint announcement](https://www.ceres.tech/newsroom/news-and-insights/doosan-fuel-cell-begins-mass-production-of-fuel-cell-power-systems-using-ceres-technology/) The 2025 annual report then showed first royalties of £110,000.[Ceres Annual Report 2025](https://www.ceres.tech/media/lponbtjc/ceres_annual-report_2025.pdf)

That mattered because it converted the business model from promise into disclosed fact. Ceres was still early in the ramp, but Doosan proved that partner manufacturing could cross the accounting threshold into royalty recognition.

## Weichai: Shareholder, Licensee, China Option

Weichai carried a different mix of strategic value. The relationship began in 2018 as a strategic partnership and equity investment centred on China, initially with a 30kW range-extender system for buses and with the prospect of wider system and stationary-power applications.[Weichai strategic partnership](https://www.ceres.tech/newsroom/news-and-insights/strategic-partnership-with-weichai-power/) Over time it became more important as a manufacturing and governance relationship. Weichai remained the largest disclosed shareholder at 19.49 per cent of issued share capital at year-end 2025, and its nominee Nannan Sun sat on the board.[Ceres Annual Report 2025](https://www.ceres.tech/media/lponbtjc/ceres_annual-report_2025.pdf) [Ceres leadership](https://www.ceres.tech/who-we-are/leadership/)

The key commercial update arrived on 5 November 2025, when Ceres announced a manufacturing licence agreement for Weichai to produce SOFC cells and stacks for stationary power in China.[Weichai manufacturing licence](https://www.ceres.tech/newsroom/news-and-insights/weichai-sign-manufacturing-licence-for-sofc-power/) That pushed Weichai from strategic option toward near-term revenue contributor.

## Delta, DENSO and Thermax: The SOEC and Data-Centre Broadening

Delta's January 2024 deal was one of the clearest signs that the platform could be sold into both power and hydrogen markets. The agreement covered technology transfer and licensing worth about £43 million and contemplated production by the end of 2026.[Delta-Ceres joint release](https://www.ceres.tech/media/ajfpxozk/180124-cwr-combined-rns-and-press-release.pdf) Delta later reinforced that commitment with a NT$6.95 billion site purchase in Taiwan for large-scale hydrogen-energy manufacturing.[Delta factory investment](https://www.ceres.tech/newsroom/news-and-insights/ceres-welcomes-delta-electronics-investment-in-factory-site-for-solid-oxide-hydrogen-energy-solutions/)

DENSO and Thermax broadened the SOEC manufacturing base geographically. DENSO's August 2024 licence agreement covered future commercial production and royalties in hydrogen applications.[DENSO licence](https://www.ceres.tech/newsroom/news-and-insights/ceres-confirms-denso-as-the-latest-licence-partner/) Thermax's September 2024 agreement gave it rights to manufacture, sell and service SOEC stack array modules, with India as an obvious strategic market.[Thermax licence](https://www.ceres.tech/news/thermax-partners-with-ceres-for-green-hydrogen-production-with-large-scale-solid-oxide-electrolysis-soec-manufacturing-in-india/)

## Shell and Centrica: Development Partner and Commercial Channel

Shell still represented validation rather than factory scale. The first green-hydrogen agreement was signed in 2022, a second-phase module-design contract followed in 2024, and first hydrogen came from Bangalore in 2025.[Ceres history](https://www.ceres.tech/who-we-are/our-history/) [Shell phase-two contract](https://www.ceres.tech/newsroom/news-and-insights/ceres-signs-contract-with-shell-for-green-hydrogen/) [Shell Bangalore milestone](https://www.ceres.tech/newsroom/news-and-insights/shell-ceres-mw-scale-electrolyser-project-produces-first-hydrogen/) That was an important proof point, but Shell had not yet been disclosed as a manufacturing licensee by the frozen date.

Centrica, by contrast, was not a manufacturer at all. Its March 2026 partnership with Ceres created a service-led route to market for multi-gigawatt on-site power in the UK and Europe, and Delta was subsequently named as the manufacturing partner in that model.[Centrica-Ceres partnership](https://www.ceres.tech/newsroom/news-and-insights/centrica-and-ceres-sign-strategic-partnership-to-bring-multi-gw-on-site-fuel-power-to-the-uk-and-europe/) [Centrica-Delta partnership](https://www.ceres.tech/newsroom/news-and-insights/centrica-and-delta-electronics-announce-partnership/)

## Revenue Stage by Partner

| Partner | Geography | Application | Revenue stage at frozen date |
|---|---|---|---|
| Bosch | Germany / Europe | SOFC stationary power | Exiting; orderly end announced in Feb 2025 |
| Doosan | South Korea | SOFC stationary power | Mass production; first royalties recognised |
| Weichai | China | SOFC stationary power | Manufacturing licence signed; licence revenue expected from FY2026 |
| Delta | Taiwan | SOFC and SOEC | Technology transfer, engineering and hardware; production targeted by end-2026 |
| DENSO | Japan | SOEC hydrogen applications | Licence, engineering and future royalties |
| Thermax | India / global | SOEC stack array modules | Licence and development stage |
| Shell | Global / India | SOEC demonstrator | Development and demonstration stage |
| Centrica | UK / Europe | Route to market for on-site power | Commercial channel, deployment dependent |

The quality of the counterparties remained striking. The shape of the stack, however, had changed. By May 2026 it was no longer accurate to describe Ceres as a British technology company reliant on four named partners. It was a Main Market-listed licensor with one partner in production, another entering manufacturing, several SOEC manufacturing relationships disclosed, and Bosch already on the way out.

chapters.title: Where Ceres sits against Bloom Energy, Plug Power, and broader fuel cell set
chapters.body:
## The Vertical Incumbent: Bloom Energy

Ceres' cleanest strategic contrast remained Bloom Energy. Bloom manufactured, sold and serviced its own solid oxide systems; Ceres licensed technology and relied on partners for manufacturing and customer access. By the frozen date Bloom's scale advantage had become larger, not smaller. Its official full-year 2025 results reported record revenue of $2.02 billion, with growth driven heavily by the AI data-centre market.[Bloom FY2025 results](https://investor.bloomenergy.com/press-releases/press-release-details/2026/Bloom-Energy-Reports-Fourth-Quarter-and-Full-Year-2025-Financial-Results-with-Record-Full-Year-Revenues/default.aspx)

The technology overlap was also broader than the older chapter implied. Bloom had not "entered" electrolysis in 2025. It unveiled the Bloom Electrolyzer in July 2021 and inaugurated a high-volume electrolyzer production line in Delaware in November 2022.[Bloom electrolyzer launch](https://investor.bloomenergy.com/press-releases/press-release-details/2021/Bloom-Energy-Unveils-Electrolyzer-to-Supercharge-the-Path-to-Low-Cost-Net-Zero-Hydrogen/default.aspx) [Bloom electrolyzer line](https://www.bloomenergy.com/news/bloom-energy-inaugurates-high-volume-electrolyzer-production-line/) That meant the Ceres-Bloom comparison now spanned both solid oxide power generation and solid oxide hydrogen production.

## How the Reference Set Looked by the Frozen Date

| Company | Model | Core technology | Latest annual revenue disclosed within the frozen window |
|---|---|---|---:|
| Ceres Power | IP licensing, engineering support, royalties | SOFC and SOEC | £32.643m (FY2025) |
| Bloom Energy | Vertical OEM and service provider | SOFC and SOEC | $2.02bn (FY2025) |
| Plug Power | Integrated hydrogen and PEM equipment platform | PEM electrolysers, fuel cells, hydrogen infrastructure | More than $700m total revenue in FY2025; equipment and related infrastructure revenue $371.1m |
| Nel | Electrolyser manufacturer | Alkaline and PEM electrolysers | NOK 963.1m revenue from contracts with customers (FY2025) |
| FuelCell Energy | Vertical OEM | Carbonate fuel cells | $158.2m total revenue (FY2025) |

The Ceres figures came from the 2025 annual report.[Ceres Annual Report 2025](https://www.ceres.tech/media/lponbtjc/ceres_annual-report_2025.pdf) Bloom's came from its February 2026 results release.[Bloom FY2025 results](https://investor.bloomenergy.com/press-releases/press-release-details/2026/Bloom-Energy-Reports-Fourth-Quarter-and-Full-Year-2025-Financial-Results-with-Record-Full-Year-Revenues/default.aspx) Plug's came from its 2025 Form 10-K and related results materials.[Plug FY2025 10-K](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1093691/000110465926022286/plug-20251231x10k.htm) [Plug FY2025 results](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1093691/000110465926022247/tm267677d1_ex99-1.htm) Nel's came from its 2025 annual report.[Nel Annual Report 2025](https://nelhydrogen.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/02/Annual-Report-2025.pdf) FuelCell Energy's came from its 2025 Form 10-K.[FuelCell Energy FY2025 10-K](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/886128/000110465925122302/fcel-20251031x10k.htm)

## The PEM and Alkaline Pack

Plug and Nel mattered because they represented the commercial mainstream of hydrogen equipment by the frozen date. Plug's 2025 filing showed more than $700 million of revenue and $371.1 million of equipment and related infrastructure sales, with electrolyser revenue helped by sales of 184 one-megawatt-equivalent units in the year.[Plug FY2025 10-K](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1093691/000110465926022286/plug-20251231x10k.htm) [Plug FY2025 results](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1093691/000110465926022247/tm267677d1_ex99-1.htm) Nel's 2025 annual report, meanwhile, showed NOK 963.1 million of revenue from contracts with customers across alkaline and PEM electrolysers.[Nel Annual Report 2025](https://nelhydrogen.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/02/Annual-Report-2025.pdf)

Those numbers did not make Plug or Nel better analogues for Ceres than Bloom was. They did show how much larger the incumbent hydrogen-supply ecosystem already was outside solid oxide. Ceres therefore had to win not only on efficiency and product architecture but on whether solid oxide could become a preferred route in selected industrial use cases rather than a technically admired niche.

## FuelCell Energy and the Carbonate Holdout

FuelCell Energy sat in a different technical family - carbonate rather than solid oxide or PEM - but it still competed for industrial decarbonisation capital, utility attention and subsidy frameworks. Its 2025 Form 10-K reported total revenue of $158.2 million and an annualised production rate of about 31.5MW.[FuelCell Energy FY2025 10-K](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/886128/000110465925122302/fcel-20251031x10k.htm) That was a reminder that not every listed fuel-cell company had scaled through the AI power narrative in the way Bloom had.

## Why Ceres Still Looked Different

The largest strategic difference was not chemistry but control. Bloom captured manufacturing margin, service economics and customer relationships directly, but paid for that with factories, working capital and a full operating footprint.[Bloom FY2025 results](https://investor.bloomenergy.com/press-releases/press-release-details/2026/Bloom-Energy-Reports-Fourth-Quarter-and-Full-Year-2025-Financial-Results-with-Record-Full-Year-Revenues/default.aspx) Plug and Nel likewise remained manufacturers, whether of PEM equipment, hydrogen infrastructure or alkaline systems.[Plug FY2025 10-K](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1093691/000110465926022286/plug-20251231x10k.htm) [Nel Annual Report 2025](https://nelhydrogen.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/02/Annual-Report-2025.pdf) FuelCell Energy continued to carry the burdens and benefits of a direct OEM model in carbonate systems.[FuelCell Energy FY2025 10-K](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/886128/000110465925122302/fcel-20251031x10k.htm)

Ceres was structurally smaller in reported revenue, but its balance sheet and operating profile were lighter because it did not fund customer factories. The price of that lightness was dependence. Partner capex, certification, product launch timing and channel development all sat outside Ceres' direct control.

## Data Centres and Hydrogen: The Two Arenas That Mattered

In power generation, Bloom had already become a direct beneficiary of hyperscale and AI data-centre demand, while Ceres was trying to reach the same market through Doosan, Delta and Centrica.[Bloom FY2025 results](https://investor.bloomenergy.com/press-releases/press-release-details/2026/Bloom-Energy-Reports-Fourth-Quarter-and-Full-Year-2025-Financial-Results-with-Record-Full-Year-Revenues/default.aspx) [Doosan joint announcement](https://www.ceres.tech/newsroom/news-and-insights/doosan-fuel-cell-begins-mass-production-of-fuel-cell-power-systems-using-ceres-technology/) [Centrica-Ceres partnership](https://www.ceres.tech/newsroom/news-and-insights/centrica-and-ceres-sign-strategic-partnership-to-bring-multi-gw-on-site-fuel-power-to-the-uk-and-europe/) In hydrogen, Plug and Nel were bigger commercial organisations but were rooted in PEM and alkaline supply, while Ceres was trying to establish solid oxide electrolysis as a differentiated route through Shell, Delta, DENSO and Thermax.[Plug FY2025 10-K](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1093691/000110465926022286/plug-20251231x10k.htm) [Nel Annual Report 2025](https://nelhydrogen.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/02/Annual-Report-2025.pdf) [Shell Bangalore milestone](https://www.ceres.tech/newsroom/news-and-insights/shell-ceres-mw-scale-electrolyser-project-produces-first-hydrogen/) [DENSO licence](https://www.ceres.tech/newsroom/news-and-insights/ceres-confirms-denso-as-the-latest-licence-partner/)

Ceres' counter-argument was that one factory platform could, in principle, supply both power and hydrogen products from the same core cell technology. The Endura launch in April 2026 stressed precisely that point, saying a single production facility could access both markets from a shared platform.[Ceres Endura](https://www.ceres.tech/newsroom/news-and-insights/ceres-launches-ceres-endura/) None of the peer comparisons made that strategic bet irrelevant; they made it more demanding.

## The Trade-Off in Full Relief

The licensing model still offered a coherent upside case. If several partners reached scale, Ceres could earn royalty revenue across multiple regions without carrying the capital intensity of a direct manufacturer. The bearish counterpoint remained equally coherent: most of the commercial leverage sat in companies other than Ceres, which meant the market would struggle to award it the same multiple as a company that controlled revenue recognition more directly.

That was the real competitive position by May 2026. Ceres was not competing to out-ship Bloom, out-build Plug or out-produce Nel on current revenue. It was competing to prove that a solid oxide IP platform could become an industry standard without owning the factories that embodied it.

chapters.title: From 2001 Imperial spin-out through partner scaling and SOEC entry
chapters.body:
## The Pivot That Defined the Decade

Ceres emerged in 2001 from Imperial College with a metal-supported solid oxide design that the company said was intended to lower temperature, improve robustness and make the technology manufacturable at scale.[Ceres history](https://www.ceres.tech/who-we-are/our-history/) The original listed-company chapter was built on a different commercial idea: direct product commercialisation. That model faltered, British Gas exited in 2012, and Phil Caldwell arrived in 2013 to reposition Ceres as a licensor rather than a manufacturer.[Ceres history](https://www.ceres.tech/who-we-are/our-history/) [Ceres leadership](https://www.ceres.tech/who-we-are/leadership/)

By the frozen date, the catalyst map had moved on from that origin story. The relevant question was no longer whether Ceres could sign industrial partners. It plainly could. The question was which disclosed events were most likely to turn the partner network into recurring revenue.

## What Had Already Happened

Several events that the older draft treated as future possibilities had already occurred. Bosch had stopped being a forward catalyst when it announced in February 2025 that it would discontinue SOFC industrialisation, seek an orderly end to the partnership and divest its 17.44 per cent stake.[Bosch statement](https://www.ceres.tech/media/ebeau4bp/ceres-statement-regarding-robert-bosch-gmbh.pdf) Doosan had moved into mass production in July 2025 and triggered first royalties.[Doosan joint announcement](https://www.ceres.tech/newsroom/news-and-insights/doosan-fuel-cell-begins-mass-production-of-fuel-cell-power-systems-using-ceres-technology/) Weichai had signed a manufacturing licence in November 2025.[Weichai manufacturing licence](https://www.ceres.tech/newsroom/news-and-insights/weichai-sign-manufacturing-licence-for-sofc-power/) Delta, DENSO and Thermax had all been publicly disclosed as manufacturing or licence partners on the SOEC side during 2024.[Delta-Ceres joint release](https://www.ceres.tech/media/ajfpxozk/180124-cwr-combined-rns-and-press-release.pdf) [DENSO licence](https://www.ceres.tech/newsroom/news-and-insights/ceres-confirms-denso-as-the-latest-licence-partner/) [Thermax licence](https://www.ceres.tech/news/thermax-partners-with-ceres-for-green-hydrogen-production-with-large-scale-solid-oxide-electrolysis-soec-manufacturing-in-india/)

In other words, the frozen-window catalyst set was no longer about unnamed optionality. It was about execution on already announced relationships.

## The Current Catalyst Board

| Catalyst | Status at frozen window | Why it mattered |
|---|---|---|
| Doosan production ramp | Mass production started in Jul 2025; first royalties booked in FY2025 | Only disclosed proof that the royalty model had crossed into production reality |
| Weichai manufacturing revenue | Licence signed in Nov 2025; 2026 contracted revenue visibility increased | Offered the next large SOFC manufacturing line after Doosan |
| Delta factory build-out | Product development under way; production targeted by end-2026; NT$6.95bn site acquired in 2025 | Linked Ceres to both data-centre power and hydrogen manufacturing scale |
| Shell to commercial SOEC | 1MW Bangalore demonstrator produced first hydrogen in 2025 | Showed technical maturity, but commercial structure was still pre-licence |
| DENSO and JERA in Japan | DENSO licence disclosed in 2024; annual report said DENSO and JERA began testing Japan's first announced SOEC hydrogen demonstrator with 35 billion yen of government funding | Added a second industrial hydrogen pathway beyond Shell |
| Thermax in India | SOEC manufacturing licence announced in Sep 2024 | Opened a large industrial market where hydrogen policy was becoming more concrete |
| Centrica channel build-out | Multi-GW partnership signed in Mar 2026; Delta added in Apr 2026 | Created a route to market for on-site power rather than another pure technology deal |

The sources for those catalysts were Ceres' own announcements and annual report.[Ceres Annual Report 2025](https://www.ceres.tech/media/lponbtjc/ceres_annual-report_2025.pdf) [Shell Bangalore milestone](https://www.ceres.tech/newsroom/news-and-insights/shell-ceres-mw-scale-electrolyser-project-produces-first-hydrogen/) [Centrica-Ceres partnership](https://www.ceres.tech/newsroom/news-and-insights/centrica-and-ceres-sign-strategic-partnership-to-bring-multi-gw-on-site-fuel-power-to-the-uk-and-europe/) [Centrica-Delta partnership](https://www.ceres.tech/newsroom/news-and-insights/centrica-and-delta-electronics-announce-partnership/)

The catalyst board also sat on top of a product and cost story. In April 2026 Ceres launched Endura, describing it as a flagship stack platform designed for resilient on-site power for data centres and other energy-intensive users, with more than 65 per cent electrical efficiency on natural gas, more than 90 per cent total efficiency in CHP, and a five-year stack life.[Ceres Endura](https://www.ceres.tech/newsroom/news-and-insights/ceres-launches-ceres-endura/) The March 2026 results statement separately said a business-transformation plan was expected to deliver 20 per cent operating-cost savings in 2026.[FY2025 final results](https://www.ceres.tech/media/jpmpucda/ceres-power-holdings-plc-final-results-statement-2026-march-26.pdf) Those were not external catalysts in the strict sense, but they shaped how quickly commercial wins could translate into operating leverage.

## The Real Forward Question

The principal catalyst was still royalty inflection, but its geography had shifted. In the earlier Bosch-centric framing, Germany had carried too much of the burden. By May 2026 the nearer-term royalty question centred on Korea first, China next, and Taiwan or Japan after that. SOEC meanwhile had moved from an abstract "hydrogen option" to a set of named manufacturing and development programmes that still needed commercial conversion.

Whether that conversion arrived before the cash balance demanded another raise remained the central question shareholders were pricing. But the chapter no longer warranted language about "no announced deal at the frozen window". There had been several announced deals. The work ahead lay in turning them into recurring economics, and in showing that Ceres could turn a broader partner set into a tighter revenue cadence.

chapters.title: SteelCell IP, SOEC IP, Imperial College heritage, patent portfolio
chapters.body:
## From Imperial Ceramics to Steel Substrate

The intellectual foundations of Ceres traced to Imperial College London. Ceres' history page said the 2001 spin-out was created to commercialise a metal-supported solid oxide fuel cell architecture based on doped-ceria electrolyte materials proposed by Professor Brian Steele.[Ceres history](https://www.ceres.tech/who-we-are/our-history/)

Steele's argument was that commercially viable solid oxide systems would need lower operating temperatures and better thermal-cycling tolerance than first-generation ceramic designs allowed. Ceres' own technology pages later framed that engineering choice as operating in a 450-630C range enabled by a steel support rather than a thick ceramic support.[Ceres cell](https://www.ceres.tech/products-and-applications/products/cell/) [Goldilocks zone](https://www.ceres.tech/newsroom/news-and-insights/the-goldilocks-zone-how-ceres-has-optimised-solid-oxide/)

## Patent Portfolio: Breadth as a Licensing Asset

A licensing model depended on defensible IP. Ceres' public materials consistently described a portfolio that covered the core metal-supported cell, stack assembly, seals, interconnects and manufacturing know-how across the jurisdictions most relevant to partners, including Europe, the US and Asia.[Ceres Annual Report 2025](https://www.ceres.tech/media/lponbtjc/ceres_annual-report_2025.pdf) [Ceres investors](https://www.ceres.tech/investors/)

That breadth mattered because Ceres was not trying to monopolise one end product. It was trying to license a platform across several product categories and geographies. The portfolio therefore had to protect not only the electrochemistry but the manufacturable system.

## The SOEC Extension

The move into electrolysis showed that the portfolio was extendable rather than exhausted. Shell's development work, Delta's 2024 licence, DENSO's 2024 licence and Thermax's 2024 agreement all rested on the proposition that the same underlying stack and manufacturing platform could be pushed into hydrogen production as well as power generation.[Shell phase-two contract](https://www.ceres.tech/newsroom/news-and-insights/ceres-signs-contract-with-shell-for-green-hydrogen/) [Delta-Ceres joint release](https://www.ceres.tech/media/ajfpxozk/180124-cwr-combined-rns-and-press-release.pdf) [DENSO licence](https://www.ceres.tech/newsroom/news-and-insights/ceres-confirms-denso-as-the-latest-licence-partner/) [Thermax licence](https://www.ceres.tech/news/thermax-partners-with-ceres-for-green-hydrogen-production-with-large-scale-solid-oxide-electrolysis-soec-manufacturing-in-india/)

## Redhill: The Engineering Campus

Redhill remained the operational centre of gravity for that IP. Ceres' factory and investor materials described a UK pilot manufacturing plant and engineering capability used to transfer technology into partner factories rather than to support a permanent in-house manufacturing footprint.[Ceres factory](https://www.ceres.tech/products-and-applications/products/factory/) [Ceres investors](https://www.ceres.tech/investors/) The 2025 annual report showed the group still investing heavily in R&D and product development even as it pushed toward commercial scale.[Ceres Annual Report 2025](https://www.ceres.tech/media/lponbtjc/ceres_annual-report_2025.pdf)

The tacit value sat in more than patent filings. It sat in process control, stack architecture, validation routines and technology-transfer experience - the sort of know-how that allowed one partner after another to move from document set to factory build-out. That remained one of Ceres' more durable but less easily quantified assets.

The public product pages also helped show what that know-how was trying to standardise. Ceres' stack page described a common building block for both fuel-cell and electrolysis operation, with listed reference metrics of 10.8kW power output, 20kg/day hydrogen production in electrolysis mode and 34.5kWh/kg efficiency in electrolysis mode.[Ceres stack](https://www.ceres.tech/products-and-applications/products/stack/) Its factory page then argued that one manufacturing template could take a partner from breaking ground to start of production in under two years while remaining adaptable for gigawatt scale.[Ceres factory](https://www.ceres.tech/products-and-applications/products/factory/) Those claims were not merely marketing details.
